study type: Mechanistic study combining human tissue analysis and animal models
exposure: AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-deficient endothelial progenitor cells
cohort: Human decidua basalis tissue from individuals with preeclampsia and animal models.
finding: Impaired functionality of endothelial progenitor cells, specifically through AMPK deficiency leading to excessive sEng secretion, contributes to the narrowing of remodeled uterine spiral arteries and reduced utero-placental perfusion, thereby elucidating a mechanism for preeclampsia pathogenesis.
